raw_response:
I farm a small piece of land, only 4.1 mu, so I do not spread money around carelessly. I start from what I know worked before, then I adjust a little. Cotton is still the crop I lean on, so I will keep the biggest share there. Maize is steady and does not fail easily, so I will keep some land in maize for grain and safety. Stevia can bring cash if it grows well, but it needs more careful looking after, so I will not put too much land into it. Wheat I will keep on a smaller piece because it is a habit here and I have well water, so I can help it at key times.

For fertilizer, I do not like to go short. If I underfeed the crop and lose yield, that hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. But with only 4.1 mu, every bag costs real money, so I will stay near what I have seen work around me. Cotton I will feed heavier than maize. Wheat I will feed enough to make heads, especially with one topdressing. Stevia I will not push too hard with nitrogen, or it grows too soft. I will use well irrigation when the crop is at a key stage, not every few days. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen people nearby get a better stand and better yield. I still keep tillage simple, mostly rotary, because on a small farm it is cheaper and easier for me to arrange.
